topics.label: Introduction and overview of the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture, outlines the learning outcomes, and establishes the framework for understanding cancer hallmarks and tumor progression.

topics.label: Sustained proliferative signaling and evasion of growth suppression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how oncogenic mutations across receptor tyrosine kinase, Wnt/beta-catenin, and TGF-beta pathways drive autonomous proliferation and override inhibitory growth controls.

topics.label: Block to terminal cell differentiation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how impaired terminal differentiation maintains cells in a proliferative state across both hematopoietic malignancies and colorectal carcinomas.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis and cell death regulation
topics.groupedBecause: It details how cancer cells evade programmed cell death through p53 pathway inactivation and altered ratios of pro- and anti-apoptotic Bcl-2 family members.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence, and cellular stress responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore telomere maintenance, senescence bypass, and p53-mediated genome protection, concluding with a synthesis of cell-autonomous cancer hallmarks.

topics.label: Metabolic reprogramming, aerobic glycolysis, and oncometabolites
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how cancer cells rewire cellular metabolism through aerobic glycolysis, tissue-of-origin metabolic adaptations, and Krebs cycle mutations that produce epigenetic modifiers.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the physiological requirement for new blood vessel recruitment to overcome oxygen diffusion limits during tumor progression.

topics.label: Mechanisms, monitoring, and genetics of tumor metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the sequential steps of metastatic dissemination, liquid biopsy monitoring via circulating tumor cells, metastatic inefficiency, and associated genomic features.

topics.label: Conclusion and summary of cancer hallmarks
topics.groupedBecause: It provides concluding remarks summarizing the multi-hallmark model of tumorigenesis and closes the lecture.
